children: Rothe Development filed for an initial public offering of its Class B common stock and applied to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The Houston-area engineering and technical services firm, which supports NASA and other federal agencies, has not previously had a public market for its securities. Titan Partners is the sole book-running manager for the offering.

Founded in 1967, Rothe Development is a mission-critical engineering, technology, operations, and technical services company serving NASA, the Department of Defense, other federal agencies, and regulated commercial markets. The company’s core capabilities span engineering and mission operations, ground systems and telemetry, IT modernization and cybersecurity, multimedia and mission communications, and ISO/IEC 17025-accredited calibration and metrology services.

Rothe operates through two reportable segments: Government Services and Commercial Services. Government Services, which generates the vast majority of revenue, includes high-profile roles supporting NASA—such as operations for the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory, mission control center video and broadcast infrastructure, and enterprise multimedia. Commercial Services focuses on precision calibration and metrology for aerospace, defense, energy, healthcare, and manufacturing clients. The company emphasizes cost-plus-fee contracts, longstanding customer relationships, specialized facilities, and a skilled workforce with security clearances as key competitive advantages.
: Large and growing demand for space exploration, national security, and critical infrastructure services across NASA, DoD, and other federal agencies.
: Increasing investment in digital infrastructure modernization, cybersecurity, AI-enabled systems, and mission-critical IT across public and private sectors.
: Longstanding incumbent on mission-critical NASA programs, including the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory and enterprise multimedia operations.
: Small and mid-sized government services contractors and business units of large aerospace and defense primes.
: Commercial space expansion, secure IT and data center modernization, advanced communications, and precision metrology needs across regulated industries.
: Principal customer is NASA; also serves DoD, MDA, and regulated commercial industries

: Headquarters in Webster, Texas; work performed at Johnson Space Center (TX), Kennedy Space Center (FL), Marshall Space Flight Center (AL), Langley Research Center (VA), and Wallops Flight Facility (VA)
: U.S.-based operations concentrated near major NASA facilities
: Multiple joint ventures including ROAR, ROAR2, RX2JV, QTS Rothe JV (conQueR), and Pabulum-Rothe JV
: Approximately 410 personnel as of December 31, 2025, including engineers and specialists with active clearances
: Portions of the workforce covered by CBAs with IAMAW, IATSE, CWA, and IBEW
: Up 7.7% year over year (FY2025 vs. FY2024)

, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman - Leads strategy and government relationships; more than five years as CEO; sole holder of Class A common stock; deep experience with NASA programs and federal contracting.

, President, Chief Operating Officer, and Director - Oversees day-to-day operations, program execution, business development, and contract management; background in ocean engineering and financial management.

, Chief Financial Officer - Joined in February 2026; extensive federal contracting finance experience; previously CFO of a Houston-based government contractor; expertise in Deltek systems and compliance.
, Independent Director Nominee - CPA and veteran finance executive across aerospace/defense; expertise in GAAP, FAR, CAS, SOX, SEC reporting; led large portfolios and ERP/FP&A transformations.
, Independent Director Nominee - Aerospace and autonomous systems leader; former CTO roles at Sidus Space and ExoTerra Resource; prior leadership at NASA, Boeing, and Rockwell.
, Independent Director Nominee - Former U.S. Congressman; served on Science and Technology Committee; experience in space, energy, transportation, and public policy.
: Approximately $2.4 million to make a one-time distribution to the Class A stockholder to repay a seller note; remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes.
